advice: err-BC-ERR-03012 and chk-3 option C both frame x=1 (or 2) of an even numerator power as a vertical tangent while ex-1 and the orientation call it a cusp. Either redraw the error on an odd numerator draw such as exponent 1/3, where the point is a vertical tangent, or drop BC-ERR-03012 from this lesson; the inferred note already flags that its scope is parametric slopes.

chk-3 option B (not differentiable because the graph has a sharp point) states a true verdict with a visual reason; as an MCQ distractor it is defensible only because the reason is scored, which a reader may find ambiguous. Consider wording it so the verdict and reason are visibly separate.

err-BC-ERR-02012 wrong step invents f'(1)=0, which is closer to BC-ERR-02014 (vertical tangent read as horizontal) than to the continuity to differentiability error; a wrong step reading 'continuous at 1, so differentiable at 1' would match the record more closely.
